title: Enterprise partner notice — limited inference glitch summary
summary: Brief partner-facing summary of a localized inference degradation on 2029-04-17 affecting hosted inference in EU-west and US-east regions. Focused on enterprise partners with dedicated traffic routing where we observed intermittent model fallbacks and elevated p95 latency for streaming sessions. This doc contains a short statuspage-ready message, a customer-facing postmortem summary, concrete mitigation steps already applied, recommended customer actions (if any), and our remediation/compensation offer for enterprise contracts.
public_statuspage_update: Status: Partial service degradation affecting inference streaming in EU-west and US-east. We are investigating increased latency and intermittent model fallbacks for a subset of tenant traffic. Impact: some requests experienced higher latency or truncated streams. Mitigation in progress. Next update within 60 minutes. — Redwood Inference
partner_direct_update: Hi <Partner Team>, summary: On 2029-04-17 22:10 UTC we detected a spike in p95 latency and intermittent model fallback for routed sessions in eu-west and us-east that impacted streamed responses for a subset of enterprise tenants. Our engineers applied targeted routing fixes and autoscaler threshold adjustments; customer-visible errors have declined and most sessions restored by 2029-04-18 01:30 UTC. We’ve prepared a concise postmortem and a short set of action items below. We will follow up with a formal SLA remediation proposal. — Aisha (Customer Success)
customer_postmortem_summary: What happened: a coordination bug between the smart-routing layer and autoscaler caused KV-cache warmups to be delayed for long-lived streaming sessions. After autoscaler-triggered placement changes, requests were temporarily routed to a compatible but higher-latency model variant (quantized v2 fallback) while the KV cache was rehydrated, which increased p95/p99 latency and led to some truncated streams. When did it start: 2029-04-17 22:10 UTC. When did core mitigation occur: 2029-04-18 00:45 UTC (targeted routing policy rollback and autoscaler configuration change). Impact: 0.6% of total requests across the affected regions experienced p95 latency > 2s for durations up to ~45 minutes; streaming truncations observed in ~0.08% of sessions. Root cause: race between routing decisions and instance lifecycle signals during scale events, leading to missed early KV pre-warm for streaming sessions. Why it matters: customers with long-lived streaming sessions or strict latency SLOs saw transient degradations and higher error rates for structured streaming outputs.
actions_we_took_immediately:
- Identified the routing->autoscaler coordination gap via trace correlation and request sampling.
- Rolled back the experimental placement policy for affected regions to a proven stable policy (2029-04-18 00:47 UTC).
- Increased KV cache rewarm priority for streaming sessions and disabled the aggressive preemption path causing cache eviction.
- Deployed a hotfix to the autoscaler to emit clearer lifecycle events and to pause routing changes until KV prewarm confirmation is received.
- Notified customers and opened support tickets for impacted tenants.
Outcome: error rates reduced to baseline and streaming stability restored by 2029-04-18 01:30 UTC.
mitigation_and_longer_term_changes:
- Ship a coordinated handshake between routing controller and instance lifecycle that requires KV-ready acknowledgment before routing switch. (PR merged: runtime/pull/5123).
- Add canary and synthetic streaming probes for every region that validate KV warm state before redirecting live traffic.
- Update autoscaler thresholds and introduce a short cooldown window for streaming-heavy instances to avoid repeated placement churn.
- Introduce telemetry alerting on model-variant fallbacks to trigger early paging for SRE/Product.
- Plan: full rollout of handshake + probes by 2029-05-10 behind a gradual canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
recommended_customer_actions:
- For partners using longest-lived streaming sessions, we recommend enabling the tenant-level 'pin-primary-node' option temporarily (instructions linked).
- Ensure client-side retry/backoff for streaming resumptions (best-practice snippet provided on the KB).
- If you experienced truncated structured outputs, please reply to this thread with the request IDs; we will prioritize log retrieval and reprocessing if possible.

estimated_customer_impact_metrics:
- Affected tenants: ~120 enterprise tenants across eu-west and us-east.
- Fraction of total requests: ~0.6% experienced elevated p95 > 2s.
- Streaming truncation rate: ~0.08% of sessions during peak window.
- Error budget consumption: estimated extra 0.03% SLA burn for impacted tenant cohort during the incident window.
compensation_and_sla_offer:
We propose the following for impacted enterprise partners:
- One-time pro-rated credit covering the incremental SLA burn for the incident window.
- Option to convert next monthly invoice to a 5% service credit if you prefer an immediate discount (to be applied upon partner approval).
- A shared technical review call with Engineering within 5 business days to walk through the root cause and roadmap for mitigations.
Next steps for acceptance: reply to this notice with preferred option and we will issue credits and schedule the review.
